one_month_reasoning: No MongoDB earnings in the window: Q3 FY27 results are due in early December 2026, and Q3/FY27 guidance was reaffirmed in the Sep 28 CEO 8-K [16]. The CEO exit (notice Sep 24, effective and announced Sep 28) and the Sep 29 investor day with its new ~3-year targets are already in the price [16][17]. The Sep 30 cooler PCE print, which cut October hike odds, is already in the $356 close (per the supervisor), so I add no macro drift. Inside the window: hyperscaler Q3 results in late October (AWS/Azure/GCP were very strong last quarter [9]) matter for sentiment only; a quick permanent CEO appointment would be mildly positive; and the $1.35B remaining buyback [18] is a small cushion that could start working now the window is open. I stay close to symmetric around $356 with about 15.5% monthly sigma, a touch below 71%/3.5 because realized vol is inflated by the two event days, and tilt the median about 0.5% up for the buyback. P(>=356) is 0.51.

fair_value.method: 50/50 blend of 40x NTM (Oct-27 to Sep-28) non-GAAP EPS of ~$9.9 ($396) and 8x NTM EV/sales on ~$4.09B of revenue plus ~$2.6B net cash over 85M fully diluted shares ($415), about $405.

Net income ~0.89x op income (20% tax plus interest income) over ~86M shares gives FY28 ~$8.3 and FY29 ~$10.6. The FY ends Jan 31, so NTM from Oct-2027 is ~1/3 FY28 + 2/3 FY29 = ~$9.9. I dropped the round-1 haircut: leadership risk sits in the multiple and the bear scenario.

Today's price is ~55x FY27 and ~43x FY28 EPS. Snowflake (+37% product revenue) and Datadog (+36%) grow faster and keep premium multiples, while MDB is guided to ~20%. SBC at ~20% of revenue, restrictive rates and the Postgres/DocumentDB threat cap the multiple, so I keep a modest de-rating to 40x NTM a year out instead of raising it.

inputs_detail.derivation: $2.41B plus ~$0.7B of FCF (80-100% conversion on ~$0.7B of op income), less ~$0.5B of buybacks from the $1.35B remaining authorization to offset SBC dilution. This pairs with a flat ~85M share count, so the buyback is not counted twice.
85.8M fully diluted weighted shares in Q2, held about flat as buybacks absorb SBC.

Current EV of ~$28B is ~8x NTM sales. It sits between Snowflake/Datadog (mid-30s growth, richer) and Elastic (15% growth, far lower). Holding 8x a year out already assumes a slight de-rating as growth settles near 20%.

bear.story: The guide-implied Q4 slowdown (+14-16%) is real, and the March 2027 FY28 guide comes in at mid-teens, the third March reset in a row. Atlas slides from ~29% toward high-teens as Postgres options inside data platforms (Snowflake Postgres, Databricks Lakebase, DocumentDB with a MongoDB API) take new workloads, and the CEO search drags on. The multiple compresses to ~5.5x sales.

base.story: MDB keeps beating its guides by a few percent, the FY28 guide is around 18-20%, and margins expand 100-200bp as targeted, putting NTM EPS near $9.9. AI-native customers add incrementally, a permanent CEO is named, and the multiple de-rates modestly to ~40x.

bull.story: The AI/agent workload wave lifting Snowflake, Datadog and the hyperscalers (AWS +37%, GCP +82%) spills into operational databases. Atlas re-accelerates above 30%, a strong permanent CEO is named, and the $1.35B buyback plus 20%+ growth push the stock back through its $473 high.

thesis_break_reason: Below about $230 (~5.5-6x NTM sales, the 52-week-low zone of $216-230), the market would most likely be pricing Atlas growth breaking below ~20% (for example a mid-teens FY28 guide in March confirming the Q4 slowdown), visible share loss to Postgres/DocumentDB, or a failed CEO succession, rather than ordinary volatility in a 70%-vol name.

reasoning: Round 2. The supervisor's corrections were arithmetic, and I verified them against the primary 8-Ks [1][16][17][18]. (1) NTM at Sep-2027 is ~1/3 FY28 + 2/3 FY29 because the FY ends Jan 31, and 150bp/yr of margin expansion on the $626M FY27 op-income guide grows EPS ~28%/yr, not 22%. NTM EPS is ~$9.9 (round 1: $9.0) and NTM revenue ~$4.09B (round 1: $3.9B). I dropped my extra leadership haircut because the multiple and the bear case already carry it. (2) Net cash is ~$2.6B, not $3.0B, when shares are held at 85M through buybacks. (3) The buyback has $1.35B remaining. (4) The investor day deck confirms 20%+ growth (up from high teens), mid-20% Atlas, +100-200bp/yr margin and 80-100% FCF conversion. It also shows FY27 guidance at ~21% op margin, +250bp. With multiples unchanged (40x P/E gives $396; 8x EV/sales gives $415), fair value rises from $385 to ~$405. I kept both multiples rather than raising them. Industry evidence is unchanged: strong chain-wide demand (hyperscalers +37-82%, Snowflake +37%, Datadog +36% [6][7][9]) versus Elastic's stalled monthly self-serve cloud (+1%) [8] and Postgres/DocumentDB products [10][11][12]. It works as a multiple cap and a bear-tail driver, not a median cut, and the supervisor agreed. The new bear fact I had not quantified is the guide-implied Q4 of +14-16% ahead of the March FY28 guide. It keeps my bear weight at 25% despite the higher fair value. Scenarios: $225/$400/$560 at 25/50/25, a mean of ~$396. Ladder: a mixture with 85% lognormal (median $370, sigma 0.45) and 15% fat-tail (median $360, sigma 0.85), trimmed at the far right tail. The median is ~$370 and P(>=356) is 0.53 (round 1: 0.50). The upside of the fair value is discounted for the March guide risk, leadership uncertainty and the 70% vol. I made no new web searches beyond re-fetching three primary SEC filings.
